verdict.rationale: Svelte's docs explicitly market components as HTML/CSS/JS you already know (svelte-docs-1, svelte-docs-4), and community feedback corroborates an easier ramp than React (svelte-comm-2, svelte-comm-8). However, the same docs reveal Svelte's reactivity relies on special rune syntax ($state, $derived, $effect, $derived.by, getter-based reactivity) that is new syntax beyond plain JS (svelte-docs-6, svelte-docs-7, svelte-docs-8, svelte-docs-20), and community notes flag it as a JS 'superset' with IDE/tooling friction and no JSX support (svelte-comm-15, svelte-comm-7). Missing for 10: independent quantified learning-curve studies, and clearer docs-side acknowledgement that runes are additional concepts beyond vanilla HTML/CSS/JS.
